verdict.oneLiner: I've never learned so much about rocks in my life.

story: Honestly, I've never learned so much about rocks in my life — their formation, creation, destruction, how they get places, how they are ever changing. Really just so lovingly done and entertainingly well done.

This show should have been a junk barrel over the top fan-service show, but it managed to keep everything together and have a lot of really great characters that all grew, learned, and became more interested in the things they started getting into as the show went on. I really think that Ruri went through such an interesting character arc, where she really was a much more interesting character by the end of the show than she was at the beginning.

For a show largely set in nature and about mining, it doesn't get environmentally preachy. It takes a much more interesting perspective of just saying "okay that's all there, now what's happening now? what can we figure out?"

Given the level of technical detail in all the adorably drawn charts and graphs, I think if you could learn and repeat back what was in the eye-catches and in the charts and graphs you would have learned more about mineralogy than 99.99999% of people, and could actually have a well informed conversation with anyone who was interested in that. So that definitely checks off the repeat viewing, and wanting to pause and read all the details.
production: The production values for the show definitely stayed consistent throughout — they made the things they wanted to be pretty look pretty, and they kept the rest of the things looking consistent. Nothing was out of sync stylistically.

A good reason for this is scripts. I cannot comment on the original manga, but the main scenario writer Michiko Yokote is literally my favorite script writer, and I didn't realize she was involved in this until ep ~2. It's hard to spot one of her works, because she does so much and has over the years, but it always has one through-line: exceedingly high quality.

body: 「光のすみか」 ("Hikari no Sumika") by Rei Yasuda.
The OP is top tier; it really sets the vibes for the show up to maximum: it's going to be casually relaxing and you are going to learn about rocks.

body: **ANN:** genres adventure, comedy, slice of life; themes CGDCT, educational, geology, mineralogy, school. Objectionable content: mild.
Studio Bind, 13 episodes, 23 minutes each, 6 July – 28 September 2025. Adapted from Keiichirō Shibuya's manga in KADOKAWA's *Harta*.
